text:
Anya: Hey team — follow-up from the RFC: I sketched a proposal for eviction tiers that ties to tenant QoS labels and runtime hints. Putting it here for quick feedback.

Devon: Nice. high-level summary?

Anya: tl;dr: instead of a single soft/hard cutoff we have 3 eviction bands (background, best-effort, production). Each band has different grace windows, reclaimable percentages, and allowed preempt paths. Runtimes can attach a hint `warmup: low|med|high` and the orch uses that to bias which tasks to prewarm vs evict.

Matt: sounds promising. how do we avoid starving background when we keep squeezing for prod spikes?

Anya: two levers: (1) per-pool min-reserve expressed in fractional GPU units (e.g., 0.1 GPU per tenant) and (2) a decay-based burst credit that replenishes slowly — background gets a stable floor, prod gets burst headroom.

Jordan: fractional GPU reserves were discussed before. Are we changing the admission surface? will tenants specify fractional quotas or do we infer?

Anya: prefer inference by default from historical qps/latency but allow explicit tenant policy overrides for enterprise customers. default flow: infer -> recommend -> apply.

SRE-Jen: operational concerns: need clear rollback if eviction aggressiveness misclassifies. Also want observability on eviction decisions per-request. Can we log an eviction_reason with trace_id?

Anya: yes — plan is to emit structured events: {decision, reason, tier, tenant, trace_id, prewarm_hint}. We'll also add an alert for sustained tail-errors after a policy flip.

Devon: what about the control plane vs operator boundary? who calculates burst credits and who enforces?

Anya: enforcement stays in the operator (close to kube/RM). Control plane (orch controller) computes target credits/parameters and pushes signed intents. Operator has final say for local safety. That prevents a flaky control plane from blowing up nodes.

Matt: example config?

Anya: pasted a mini example (not final):
```
eviction:
  bands:
    - name: background
      grace: "120s"
      reclaimable_pct: "30"
      preempt_path: "cold-evict"
    - name: best-effort
      grace: "30s"
      reclaimable_pct: "60"
      preempt_path: "hot-swap"
    - name: production
      grace: "5s"
      reclaimable_pct: "100"
      preempt_path: "immediate-preempt"
burst_credits:
  replenish_rate: "0.05" # fractional GPU per minute
  max_window: "3600s"
```

Jordan: thanks. a couple questions: (A) how do we test this in canary without impacting latency-sensitive tenants? (B) should we add a "safety dampener" that forbids >X% change to reclaimable_pct per rollout?

Anya: answers: (A) canary uses tenant-safe flags: we run policy in dry-run mode for a slice, emit metrics and compare predicted vs actual evictions; then enable for synthetic tenants, then opt-in customers. (B) yes, operator-level dampener — e.g., max_delta_per_hour and a pinned fallback policy.

SRE-Jen: add automated chaos scenarios in staging — simulate sudden spike + node-loss and ensure fallback to pinned model variants so we don't thundering herd the control plane.

Devon: what about cost accounting? fractional reserves complicate billing. we need a mapping from fractional GPU usage to billing units and visible metrics per route.

Anya: agreed. we'll emit per-tenant amortized GPU-seconds and show the effective utilization vs reserved. billing can be derived from that. Also proposal: when we infer reserves, include a confidence score so finance/sales can opt for manual commit.

Jordan: quick nit: prefer "preempt_path" values to be enum-like: COLD, HOT_SWAP, FORCED so operator code is simpler.

Anya: yep will update.

Matt: rollout checklist suggestion:
- dry-run for 48h on small slice (metric: predicted_evictions vs actual)
- synthetic load tests: 1000x spike to validate backoff
- enable operator dampeners + pinned fallback
- observability dashboards + runbook updates

SRE-Jen: add an alert for >2x background tail-latency increase sustained for 5m after policy changes.

Devon: thanks all. I'll spin up a small RFC follow-up doc with the updated enums and the operator handshake details. Can someone volunteer to own the canary harness?

Matt: I can take the canary harness with Jordan. We'll start with a synthetic tenant set.

Anya: perfect — assigning to Matt/Jordan. I'll update the proto and push a draft to the RFC thread. deploy-bot: created branch rfc/eviction-bands-7276

deploy-bot: Branch rfc/eviction-bands-7276 pushed by Anya. CI checks passed.

Jordan: great, closing loop — we'll track progress on the RFC and schedule an ops dry-run next week. :thumbsup:
